stories.title: The good news out of Cop31? That most of the world’s governments said no to an agreement stripped of meaning | Bill Hare
stories.summary: Co-chairing global climate talks is clearly not something to be repeated, certainly not by Australia, which is exporting climate pain The failure of Cop31 in Antalya was a line in the sand moment, a victory for multiculturalism as countries stood up to the big fossil fuel producers and said no. The text they rejected barely recognised the catastrophic climate emergency we’re facing, let alone signalled a definitive move away from fossil fuels. The good news is that most of the world’s governments rejected an agreement stripped of meaning. And the power of one particular fossil fuel producer, Saudi Arabia, needs particular scrutiny. What we also know is that co-chairing global climate talks is clearly not something to be repeated, certainly not by Australia. It didn’t work. Continue reading...

stories.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
stories.summary: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains. Continue reading...

stories.summary: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia. The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions. Continue reading...

stories.title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
stories.summary: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report. In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund ( UNFPA ) published on Thursday. Continue reading...

stories.title: Muru
stories.summary: Muru Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi 20 years ago, and has been thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production ever since. Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production. As he did with wrapture , he's been publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the project as he works on it - as part of his development process. Here's everything he's published so far, all in the last three weeks: 2026-11-04 — Twenty years of mod_wsgi, and what comes next 2026-11-05 — A first look at Muru 2026-11-07 — Muru: looking inside the workers 2026-11-08 — Muru: how it fits together 2026-11-09 — Muru: import once, fork many 2026-11-10 — Muru: HTTPS in development 2026-11-11 — Muru: WSGI and ASGI together 2026-11-11 — AI as a lifestyle choice 2026-11-12 — Muru: releases, not restarts 2026-11-13 — Muru: canaries without a service mesh 2026-11-14 — Muru: a better tenant in a container 2026-11-15 — Muru: working with Kubernetes, not around it 2026-11-16 — Muru: scaling from what the workers report 2026-11-17 — Muru: scaling to zero 2026-11-18 — Muru: overlays on a schedule 2026-11-19 — Muru: noticing and responding 2026-11-20 — Muru: a toolbar on every page 2026-11-21 — Muru: tracing in the toolbar 2026-11-22 — Muru: when lazy imports help That post about AI as a lifestyle choice is particularly worth a read: The AI may be doing a lot of the work on the surface, but deciding what isn't good enough yet is still down to me, and twenty years of getting things wrong with mod_wsgi turns out to be useful for that. I am prepared to put in the hard work to keep polishing Muru until it is something I would trust, and something you would too. Quoting Levent Alpöge
stories.summary: I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too. Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions. It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater. [...] Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line. — Levent Alpöge , alpo.ge/remark.pdf Tags: anthropic , claude , generative-ai , mathematics , ai , llms , levent-alpoge
